sections: Do technical indicators work the same for Synthetic Indices?
sources.assessment: Provider describes CSPRNG generation and no price-setting order book. Applying ICT liquidity terminology does not establish observed resting market orders.
sources.limits: Not a proof of IID price levels, a martingale, or impossibility of every profitable trading policy; no change to the Boom/Crash scope. Current indicative spreads were not substituted into history.

sources.assessment: Provider describes tick-based probabilities, average event intervals and native spike/drift directions.
sources.limits: An average interval is not a scheduled next event. Marketing strategy suggestions are not measured predictive or payoff evidence.

sections: How traders can plan for spike behaviour
sources.assessment: Provider states tick independence and no overdue-event increase merely from waiting; a stop is a trigger and can fill at a different next available price.
sources.limits: Attributed provider statement, not an independent generative-model audit or universal profit theorem. Illustrative images are not price data.

sources.assessment: Derived CFD entry and Boom/Crash exit use a tick after server processing; spreads can widen and execution delay exists.
sources.limits: Does not verify our public-feed-to-CFD mapping, account-specific costs or exact-second research fill proxy. No real or demo orders were used to test execution.

sources.assessment: Public tick data is documented without authentication; concrete observed field availability comes from the saved controlled capture.
sources.limits: Neither documentation nor a 240-message capture inventories every possible endpoint or establishes executable CFD bid/ask history.
